video.title: I Tried to Make $10K in 10 Days With Costco Returns

summary: Chris Koerner flies in Shannon, an experienced liquidation reseller, to teach him to buy Costco customer-return pallets via the B-Stock auction platform and resell them on Facebook Marketplace. They bid on two lots (18 pallets of appliances at about $243/unit and a 12-unit patio/shed/gazebo lot at about $222/unit landed) and then test, photograph, list and sell the items. Chris aimed for $10K profit in 10 days but took 12.5 days; exact final totals are not stated in the transcript. Key lessons: buy at a very low per-unit cost, list the best items first for momentum, respond fast, and cut prices when listings get no hits. This is hands-on physical work, not hands-off.

ideas.name: Costco return pallet flipping via B-Stock auctions
ideas.one_liner: Buy Costco customer-return lots at auction for roughly 10-20% of retail and resell items individually on Facebook Marketplace.
ideas.business_model: One-off resale margin on liquidation goods
ideas.customer: Local consumers on Facebook Marketplace looking for discounted appliances, patio furniture, grills and sheds
ideas.problem: Consumers want big-ticket items cheaper than retail; Costco needs to offload returns and excess stock
ideas.offer: Brand new or like-new appliances and outdoor items at roughly 50-70% of retail with local pickup or free delivery nearby and a 14-30 day goodwill support promise

pricing.model: Price at about 50-70% of retail; cut price if no hits; set an aggressive price and explain why for flawed items
pricing.notes: Shannon suggests worst-case comps from Facebook Marketplace and sells at 50-70% of retail; first-day prices may be underpriced.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook Marketplace listings with video first, up to 12 photos showing positives and flaws, ChatGPT-written SEO titles and descriptions, a personal credibility line, model number, colour and condition, and free delivery within 5-10 miles. Shannon says Whatnot is good for food.

quote.text: You can set up a chat GPT. Say, "Hey, create me an SEO based Facebook marketplace ad. Make sure you list all the features
quote.speaker: Shannon

ideas.delivery: Owner personally receives pallets in a garage or shop, cuts them open, tests electrics, cleans, photographs, lists, answers Messenger chats, and hands over locally or delivers; heavy items are moved by hand, with help from friends.
unit_economics_claims: Lot 1 cost about $243 per unit landed against Costco price of about $1,150 per unit
Lot 2 cost about $2,600 for 12 units (about $222 per unit incl. freight) with $13,000 retail value
Shannon says tripling money is conservative and 2x is worst case
Chris took 12.5 days instead of 10 to reach the goal; totals not stated
ideas.startup_cost: Credit card or net-30 terms; the two lots cost roughly $5,600 plus about $130/month for a storage unit if needed
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Within a few days of the pallets arriving; first sale was within a day or so of listing

acquisition.how: Listing creation can be AI-assisted (ChatGPT titles and copy), but Facebook Marketplace has no sanctioned API for posting, and photos and video must be taken physically.

onboarding.how: Messenger chats can use templates, but buyers ghost and haggle, and pickup times need human coordination.

delivery.how: Physical pallets must be received, unwrapped, tested, cleaned, photographed, stored and handed over or delivered by a person.

billing.how: Cash and Venmo at handover, taken in person.

support.how: Occasional post-sale problems handled by the owner personally as goodwill; low volume but needs a human.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has equivalents (B-Stock UK, Costco UK liquidation pallets, Facebook Marketplace, eBay, Gumtree), but the Costco returns lots on B-Stock are US-centred. UK Consumer Rights Act applies to sales of used goods by traders, and sellers who resell regularly are trading, so need HMRC registration; electrical goods need PAT or safety care. Garage space and UK-sized appliances differ from the US.

risks: Condition grade uncertainty: some items arrive broken, missing parts or damaged
Heavy, bulky stock needs space, vehicles and manual labour
Capital tied up and storage costs if items do not sell
Items like sheds may not sell (the shed went unsold)
Speaker-promoted course and mastermind may bias claims

tactics.name: Check worst-case resale comps before bidding
steps: Look up the item on Facebook Marketplace within about 80 miles of your area
Use the conservative figure and aim to get your investment back fast
Target a landed price of about $200-250 per unit for mixed big-ticket lots

quote.text: You want to look like, okay, what's worst case scenario.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Choose lots by manifest and condition grade
steps: Read the manifest for unit count, retail prices and low average bid per unit
Prefer 'used good' returns and new; avoid 'used fair' and 'mixed'
Look for photos showing items still in boxes with factory stickers
Prefer categories with demand and barriers such as appliances, outdoor gear and Blackstone grills

tactics.name: List the best items first for momentum
steps: Test and list the best items on arrival day
Defer fixes like broken doors and cleaning
Get an early sale to reinforce motivation and recover capital

quote.text: I like to say focus is overrated. momentum is underrated.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: High-converting Facebook Marketplace listing
steps: Put a 60-second walk-around video first
Use all available photo slots including flaws and install kit
Have ChatGPT write an SEO title and description with model number and colour
Add a personal credibility sentence
State the retail price and link to it
Offer free delivery within 5-10 miles
Create separate listings per item or colour

tactics.name: Messenger response and negotiation
steps: Reply fast with a call to action, such as a specific pickup time
Use text expander templates ending with availability
Say you have other inquiries and will follow up Monday
Offer a small discount for same-day pickup or delivery
If no hits after correct keywords and category, boost then cut price

quote.text: Always end the templated thing or the message with, "Okay, I'm available Saturday from 10:00 to 1.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Frame flawed items honestly
steps: Disclose scratches, dents and missing parts clearly
Say it is priced aggressively because of the flaw and link to retail price
Keep a complete item next to the flawed one when selling in person

warnings.warning: Avoid 'used fair' and 'mixed' grades; mixed can be anything and salvage can be mostly poor.
Customer returns are not tested in the warehouse, so expect at least one defective unit in a load.

quote.text: almost certainly means that at least one of them will have something wrong.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Procrastinating on listing and slow responses delayed Chris's goal beyond 10 days.
Underpricing at first can signal that you priced too low; new sellers often panic-discount.
Assembled sheds are unattractive because of the many screws and the shed did not sell.

lessons.lesson: Buy at a very low per-unit price relative to worst-case resale so a single sale can return the investment.

quote.text: You could sell one item and get your investment back.
quote.speaker: Shannon

lessons.lesson: Momentum beats perfection: list the easy winners first rather than getting stuck fixing problem items.
Speed of response and willingness to cut prices matter more than perfecting listings.
Honest framing of flaws increases buyer trust and conversion.
Hands-off this is not; the business is physical problem-solving and logistics.
Local reputation and a goodwill return window can differentiate you and create referrals.
Test unfamiliar niches with a modest lot first; surprising items like garment steamers sold fastest.
Carrying costs such as storage mean slow stock should be discounted or cleared rather than held.

evidence_quality.rationale: Chris is the novice in this experiment and Shannon's income claims are unverified. Final revenue and profit figures were removed from the transcript ('that much'), so the headline outcome cannot be checked. Per-unit costs and listing prices are specific and first-hand.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Shannon sells a mastermind (2,200 members) and the 'flip system'; Chris promotes TK Owners community and TKOS podcast submissions.
